My family has about 10 mu of contracted land here in Quzhou. Flat ground, decent loamy soil, a pump well shared with a few neighbors. I've been farming this same plot since I took it over from my father about eight years ago.

There's really no question what I'm planting — winter wheat followed by summer maize, same as every year, same as everyone else around here. Two crops on the same land. The wheat goes in around the National Holiday in October, comes out in June. Then I turn around and get maize in the ground within a week of harvest. That's how you squeeze two harvests out of one year.

For wheat, I'll buy Jimai 22 seed from the county co-op — it's subsidized and I know it does well here. Before planting I'll rotary till the maize stubble under, put down compound fertilizer (diammonium phosphate plus some potash), then drill the seed. In March when it starts jointing I'll topdress with urea. Water four times: before the ground freezes in November, again at jointing in March, at heading in April, and a grain-fill water in May if it's dry. Herbicide in November for the broadleaf weeds, fungicide spray in May for powdery mildew and scab, one more spray for aphids if they show up bad. I'd expect to pull around 450 jin per mu — call it 450 kg.

For maize I'll go with Zhengdan 958 hybrid — reliable, the seed dealer pushes it and I've seen good stands with it. No need to till again, I'll just plant straight into the wheat stubble rows. Fertilizer goes in as compound at planting and urea topdress at the 6-leaf stage. The summer rains usually handle most of the water need but I'll irrigate twice — once around silking if it's dry, once more if the grain fill period looks stressed. Herbicide right after emergence, and I'll watch for armyworm in July — one spray if I see them. Expecting around 580 kg per mu.

I'm not trying anything new this year. Cotton prices are unpredictable and I don't have the equipment. Vegetables need too much hand labor. Wheat and maize: I know the costs, I know roughly what I'll get, and I know who will buy it.
